scenes.onScreen: "Check, then shine": three numbered lines (1. Tests keep money code honest; 2. assertRaises checks that bad input is rejected; 3. f-string alignment makes a neat report) and an analogy card: a final inspection before the shop opens: everything checked, then polished

scenes.narration: Money code deserves tests. We write a test case with a few checks. Assert equal for exact answers. Assert raises, as a context manager, to check that bad input raises the right error. Run the tests after every change. Then polish the report. Inside an f string, a colon, a less than sign and a number left aligns text in a column. A greater than sign right aligns, and dot two f shows two decimals. Think of a final inspection before the shop opens. Everything is checked, then polished.

scenes.narration: Here is why we test. Imagine you change the money function next month. Without tests, you hope nothing broke. With tests, you run them. In a second you see a green tick, or a red cross with the name of the failed test. The net catches the fall before your users see it. Good tests are small, fast, and each checks one thing, with a name that says what.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: a test that always passes
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The test passes, and the function is wrong. It turns point two nine into twenty eight. The test compares the result with the same function called again, so it can never fail. A test needs a known answer, written by you. Compare with twenty nine, and the bug is caught at once.

props.why: A test must compare against an independent, known answer. Comparing a result with the same function's result can never fail, so it proves nothing.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the test never fail? It was always comparing itself with itself.

shorts.title: Test money code
shorts.script: Money code deserves tests. Write a test case with unittest. Assert equal checks exact answers. Point two nine must become twenty nine cents. Run the tests after every change. Then old bugs do not come back. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Test your money code.

shorts.title: assertRaises
shorts.hook: "To test that bad input is rejected, use assert raises, as a with block."
shorts.script: To test that bad input is rejected, use assert raises, as a with block. If the code inside raises a value error, the test passes. If it does not raise, the test fails. It checks the error, not just the answer. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Test the errors too.

shorts.title: Align columns
shorts.hook: "Make reports tidy with f string formats."
shorts.script: Make reports tidy with f string formats. Colon, less than, ten, left aligns in ten columns. Greater than aligns right. And dot two f shows two decimals. Together, the columns line up like a real table. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Line up the columns.

shorts.title: Useless test
shorts.hook: "A test that always passes is worse than no test."
shorts.script: A test that always passes is worse than no test. Comparing a result with the same function's result can never fail. A real test compares with a known answer you wrote yourself. Then a wrong function fails the test. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Compare with a known answer.
